rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a thermal treatment to enhance coherency, while the paper varied the modulation period (λ) by sputtering to create different interface types (coherent, semicoherent, grain-boundary-dominated). This is a different kind of intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies creep at 400–600°C and 80% of yield stress, whereas the paper used room-temperature nanoindentation creep at 5 mN with varying loading rates. These are completely different regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes coherent boundaries blocking dislocation climb/glide. The paper's mechanism for the most creep-resistant sample involves semicoherent interfaces promoting interfacial amorphization and diffusion/interface-slip creep, not coherent boundaries blocking dislocations.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower creep rates for enhanced coherency. The paper found the lowest creep rate and a diffusion/interface-slip mechanism for the semicoherent (M16) sample, not the coherent (M8) one. The predicted direction relative to the baseline is opposite.
